title: TAXI: Traveling Salesman Problem Accelerator with X-bar-based Ising Macros Powered by SOT-MRAMs and Hierarchical Clustering
problem: Ising solvers with hierarchical clustering for large-scale Traveling Salesman Problems (TSPs) face quality degradation as problem size scales beyond certain extent. Hardware-agnostic approaches underutilize available hardware resources.
motivation: TSP is a fundamental NP-hard optimization problem; Ising solvers promise scalability, but existing methods degrade solution quality at scale and miss hardware co-design opportunities.
method: TAXI uses crossbar (X-bar) based Ising macros solving TSP subproblems via hierarchical clustering without inter-macro data movement, enabling massive parallelism. Spin-Orbit-Torque (SOT) MRAM devices serve as compact, energy-efficient random number generators enabling rapid natural annealing within each macro.
key_novelty: Hardware-algorithm co-design combining Ising solver macros with SOT-MRAM-based random annealing and hierarchical clustering to achieve massive parallelism without inter-macro data movement.
contributions: Crossbar-based Ising macro architecture with independent TSP subproblem solving
SOT-MRAM devices as compact random number generators for natural annealing
Hardware-algorithm co-design preserving solution quality to 85,900-city TSPs
8x speedup over state-of-the-art clustering-based Ising solver; solutions 20-22% from optimal
limitations: Solution quality remains 20-22% suboptimal; scalability limits relative to exact solvers for small instances.
primary_theme: In-memory crossbar Ising solver with SOT-MRAM annealing for large-scale TSP
